meta.climate: Winter 0-10°C, Summer 15-25°C, Monsoon July-Sept, Frost Nov-Feb

overview.totalFoodSelfSufficiency: ~70-80%. You grow milk, eggs, vegetables, grains, fruit, honey. You buy rice, salt, oil, spices, tea.
overview.gardenSize: 0.5-1 acre kitchen garden + 0.5 acre fodder crops for animals
overview.keyPrinciple: Grow what the altitude gives you. Don't fight the climate — work with it.
overview.soil: Kumaon soil is fertile but rocky. Amend with cow dung compost. Terracing may be needed on slopes.

yearRound.name: Year-Round Crops (grow in any season with basic protection)

crops.use: Saag, saag paneer, salads, smoothies, cooking green
crops.notes: Frost actually makes it sweeter. Plant in succession every 2 weeks for continuous harvest.

crops.use: Saag, pickled greens, oil from seeds
crops.notes: THE winter vegetable of Kumaon. Grows when nothing else does. Seeds produce mustard oil too.
30 days from seed to harvest. Fastest crop you can grow. Plant every 2 weeks.
Can grow from kitchen scraps — put root end in water, then soil.
Methi grows in 21 days. Coriander bolts in heat — grow in shade in summer.

spring.name: Spring (March-May) — Planting Season
spring.description: Soil warms up. Last frost in March-April. Time to plant everything.

crops.use: Staple carb. Aloo gobi, paratha, chips, everything.
crops.notes: Native to Himalayas. Perfect for your altitude. Plant seed potatoes 4 inches deep, 12 inches apart.

crops.use: Fresh eating, matar paneer, frozen for later
crops.notes: Cool-season crop. Plant early. Vines need staking.

crops.use: Sabzi, salads, dried beans for storage
crops.notes: Bush beans are easier than pole beans. Succession plant every 3 weeks.

crops.use: Rajma-chawal — the Kumaon staple. Protein source.
crops.notes: Traditional Kumaon crop. Grows in monsoon. Dry and store for year-round use.
Needs warm soil. Can grow on trellis to save space.
Vine — needs trellis or fence. Very productive.
Vine — spreads on ground. Store whole for months.

summer.name: Summer (June-August) — Peak Growing + Monsoon
summer.description: Warmest months. Monsoon rain from July. Abundant growth.

crops.notes: Start seedlings indoors in Feb, transplant after last frost. Stake plants. Indeterminate varieties keep producing.
Heat-loving. Productive all summer.

crops.crop: Bottle Gourd / Ridge Gourd / Bitter Gourd
crops.notes: Vine crops. Monsoon is peak season. Trellis needed.
Perennial in your climate — can survive winter if protected. Plant once, harvest for years.
Named after Shimla for a reason — grows well at altitude.

monsoon.name: Monsoon (July-September) — Rain-Fed Crops
monsoon.description: Heavy rain. Plant water-loving crops. Protect existing plants from waterlogging.

crops.notes: Monsoon is perfect for rajma. Dry the beans and store — they last all year.

crops.use: Roti, porridge, malt drink. Highly nutritious.
crops.notes: Ancient Kumaon grain. Drought-tolerant once established. Traditional staple.

crops.use: Porridge, pulao, kheer. Light, easy to digest.
crops.notes: Traditional Kumaon grain. Grows in wet conditions. Stores well.
Fast-growing — 60-80 days. Good catch crop.
Perennial. Plant once, harvest for years. Takes 8-10 months to mature. High value.

crops.use: Fresh ginger, dried powder, tea, medicinal
crops.notes: Grows in shade. Plant under trees or shade cloth. High value crop.

autumn.name: Autumn (September-November) — Harvest + Plant Winter Crops
autumn.description: Main harvest season. Also time to plant winter crops. Preserve food for winter.

crops.use: Gobi paratha, aloo gobi, gobi manchurian
crops.notes: Cool-season crop. Cover with leaves if frost comes early.
Very cold-hardy. Can stay in ground through light frost.

crops.use: Salads, gajar ka halwa, cooking, juice
crops.notes: Sweet in cold weather. Leave in ground — frost makes them sweeter.
Cold-hardy. Stores well in sand for months.
Very cold-hardy. Grows in frost.
Plant in autumn, harvest in spring. Stores for months after harvest.

crops.use: Cooking staple. Ranikhet red onion is famous.
crops.notes: Traditional Kumaon variety. Plant sets (small bulbs) in autumn.

winter.name: Winter (November-February) — Cold-Hardy Crops + Preservation
winter.description: Frost from November. Snow possible at your altitude. Grow cold-hardy greens. Preserve summer harvest.

crops.notes: Frost makes it sweeter. THE winter green. Can grow under simple plastic cover.

crops.use: Sarson ka saag, pickles, oil from seeds
crops.notes: Grows when nothing else does. Frost-tolerant. THE Kumaon winter crop.
Winter peas are sweeter than summer peas. Grow under shade cloth.
Cold-hardy varieties. Can grow in pots on windowsill too.
Bolts in heat — winter is the best time to grow it.

fodderCrops.name: Fodder Crops (Feed Your Animals)
fodderCrops.description: Grow your own animal feed. Reduces cost, keeps animals healthy.

crops.use: Primary green fodder for cow and sheep
crops.notes: Drought-tolerant. Cut 2-3 times per season. THE fodder crop.

crops.season: Plant Sep-Oct and Feb-Mar, harvest year-round
crops.use: High-protein green fodder. Best for dairy cows.
crops.notes: Perennial. Cut every 25-30 days. Nitrogen-fixer — improves soil.

crops.season: Plant Feb-Mar, cut year-round after establishment
crops.use: Tall grass fodder for cows and sheep
crops.notes: Perennial. Plant once, cut for years. Very high yielding.

crops.use: Fodder + grain for you and animals
crops.notes: Dual purpose — humans eat the grain, animals eat the stalk.

perennialPlants.name: Perennial Plants (Plant Once, Harvest for Years)
perennialPlants.description: Long-term investments. Plant in year 1, harvest from year 3-5 onwards.

plants.use: Fresh eating, juice, cider, drying, preserves
plants.notes: Kumaon is famous for apples. Plant 3-5 trees. Choose local varieties (Red Delicious, Royal Delicious, Golden).
Long-term investment. Kumaon walnuts are famous. Take years but produce for decades.
Plant once, harvest rhizomes, replant some for next year. High value.
Needs shade. Grow under trees. High value.

medicinalHerbs.name: Medicinal Herbs (Himalayan Speciality)
medicinalHerbs.description: Grow your own supplements. The Himalayas are the pharmacy.

herbs.growing: Plant Feb-Mar, harvest Nov-Dec. Root is the medicine.
herbs.notes: Easy to grow. Drought-tolerant. Dry the roots, powder them. Premium supplement crop.

herbs.growing: Plant year-round in moist soil. Perennial ground cover.
herbs.notes: Grows near water. Good ground cover for moist areas.

herbs.growing: Plant year-round. Perennial in your climate.
herbs.notes: Grows like a weed. Dry leaves for tea. Sacred plant — you'll have it everywhere.

herbs.growing: Plant Mar-Apr. Perennial in frost-free areas.
herbs.notes: 300x sweeter than sugar. Dry leaves, crush, use as sweetener. High value crop.
Grows fast, spreads. Cut-and-come-again. Makes excellent tea.

methods.what: Tomatoes, chillies, herbs, turmeric, ginger, fruits
methods.cost: Free — just sunshine and clean trays
methods.notes: Himalayan sun is intense at altitude — perfect for drying. Make sun-dried tomatoes, dried herbs, dried chillies.

methods.what: Mango, lime, chilli, carrot, mixed vegetables
methods.notes: Indian pickles last 6-12 months. Make in summer, eat all year.

methods.what: Potatoes, carrots, beetroot, turnip, garlic, onion
methods.cost: Free — just a cool, dark, dry space
methods.notes: Dig a pit or use an under-stair storage. Root vegetables store 3-6 months in sand.

methods.what: Peas, beans, greens, herbs (in oil or water)
methods.notes: Best quality preservation. Freeze summer abundance for winter.
Ghee from cow milk lasts 6-12 months without refrigeration. Curd and cheese are daily.

january.vegetables: Spinach, mustard greens, radish, peas (winter crops)
january.grains: Stored rajma, madua, jhangora from autumn harvest

february.vegetables: Spinach, mustard, radish, start planting spring crops
february.note: Start seedlings indoors for March transplant

march.milk: Cow (fresh milk if just calved) + goat
march.vegetables: Spring planting begins. Peas, beans, potatoes going in.

april.vegetables: Peas, radish, spinach, herbs. Plant tomatoes, peppers.

july.vegetables: Ridge gourd, bitter gourd, pumpkin, tomatoes

august.vegetables: Full monsoon harvest. Plant autumn crops.

september.vegetables: Tomatoes, beans, gourds. Plant winter crops.
september.note: Start preserving — dry tomatoes, make pickles

october.vegetables: Cauliflower, cabbage, carrot, beetroot. Harvest potatoes.

november.note: Store root vegetables in cellar. Dry herbs.

december.note: Winter greens + stored food. Rest and plan.
